# EDA findings (auto-generated by src/02_eda.py)

## Price & size analysis

**Q1 Price distribution:** Price ranges 10-500 lakhs, mean 254.6, median 253.9, skew 0.01. The histogram is essentially flat (uniform), unlike real markets which are right-skewed.

**Q2 Size distribution:** Size ranges 500-5000 sq ft, mean 2750, median 2747, skew 0.00; also near-uniform.

**Q3 Price/sqft by property type:** median INR/sqft - Apartment: 9,245, Independent House: 9,305, Villa: 9,190. Kruskal-Wallis p=0.019, but the gap between types is only 1.3% - statistically detectable with 250k rows yet practically negligible.

**Q4 Size vs price:** Pearson r=-0.003, Spearman rho=-0.003 - effectively zero. In a real market larger homes cost more; here size does not explain price.

**Q5 Outliers:** IQR rule flags 19,723 rows (7.9%) as price/sqft outliers (max 99,182 INR/sqft vs median 9,245); 0 outliers for size and price (both are bounded/uniform). PPSF outliers arise from small flats with high prices - they are flagged, not removed.

## Location-based analysis

**Q6 Avg price/sqft by state:** highest Karnataka (13,252), lowest Punjab (12,931); the spread between states is only 2.5%. Kruskal p=0.582 -> no statistically significant difference.

**Q7 Avg price by city:** range 250.8-258.5 lakhs (Cuttack lowest, Bangalore highest) - a spread of only 3.1% across 42 cities. Note the x-axis is truncated at 240 to make differences visible.

**Q8 Median age by locality:** median age per locality ranges 16-21 yrs (overall median 18); differences are small and consistent with sampling noise.

**Q9 BHK across cities:** every city has a near-uniform mix - each BHK category is 19-22% of a city's listings (ideal uniform = 20%).

**Q10 Price trends, top-5 localities:** top 5 by average price/sqft: Locality_207, Locality_416, Locality_246, Locality_359, Locality_387. The dataset has NO transaction dates, so true price trends cannot be computed; the chart uses year-built cohorts as a proxy and shows no consistent upward trend (lines cross and are noisy).

## Feature relationships & correlation

**Q11 Correlations:** strongest pairs: Size_in_SqFt~Price_per_SqFt_INR (-0.61); Nearby_Schools~Infrastructure_Score (+0.60); Nearby_Hospitals~Infrastructure_Score (+0.60); Floor_No~Total_Floors (+0.58). Apart from mechanical relationships (price/sqft is derived from price and size; infrastructure score from schools/hospitals; total vs floor number), all other pairs have |r| < 0.01.

**Q12 Schools vs price/sqft:** Spearman rho=-0.002 (p=0.26) - no relationship.

**Q13 Hospitals vs price/sqft:** Spearman rho=-0.002 (p=0.39) - no relationship.

**Q14 Price by furnished status:** mean lakhs - Furnished: 254.4, Semi-furnished: 254.3, Unfurnished: 255.0. Kruskal p=0.609 -> no statistically significant difference.

**Q15 Price/sqft by facing:** mean INR/sqft - East: 13,024, North: 13,025, South: 13,044, West: 13,140. Kruskal p=0.346 -> no statistically significant difference.

## Investment, amenities & ownership

**Q16 Owner type:** Broker: 83,479, Owner: 83,268, Builder: 83,253 (near-equal thirds).

**Q17 Availability:** Under_Construction: 125,035, Ready_to_Move: 124,965. The 'Sold' status listed in the data dictionary does not occur in the file.

**Q18 Parking vs price:** with parking 254.7 vs without 254.4 lakhs (diff +0.32); Mann-Whitney p=0.575.

**Q19 Amenities vs price/sqft:** Clubhouse: 13,070 vs 13,041 (p=0.92); Garden: 13,065 vs 13,049 (p=0.73); Gym: 13,097 vs 12,999 (p=0.02); Playground: 13,049 vs 13,072 (p=0.99); Pool: 13,073 vs 13,037 (p=0.37). Differences are under 1% (the Gym p-value is borderline and, with 5 tests, not convincing) - no amenity carries a meaningful premium.

**Q20 Transport access:** avg INR/sqft - Low 13,086, Medium 13,062, High 13,027 (Kruskal p=0.61). Good-Investment share (model label, which rewards infrastructure by construction): Low 23.5%, Medium 30.1%, High 36.7%.

## Additional analyses requested in the project brief

**E1 Area vs investment return:** corr(size, projected CAGR)=+0.440; share of Good Investments by size quintile: XS 9.0%, S 19.8%, M 30.4%, L 40.5%, XL 50.9%. Caution: price is independent of size in this data, so a bigger home at the same price has a lower price/sqft and looks 'undervalued' versus the city median. The growth model rewards that, so this rising pattern is a label-construction effect, not market evidence.

**E2 Crime rate vs investment:** the dataset has **no crime-rate column**, so this cannot be measured directly. The closest available safety proxy is the `Security` flag; Good-Investment rate with security 32.2% vs without 28.0%. A real crime-rate feed (e.g. NCRB district data) should be joined before drawing conclusions.

**E3 Infrastructure vs resale value:** corr(infrastructure score, current price)=-0.001 (none). Projected 5-yr value does rise with infrastructure, but that is the growth model's assumption (+/-1.5pp), not an empirical finding.
